_about: Learning profile defaults, one per source, keyed kind/name. Read by learn/source_profile.py; a person's own choices (consent.sh mode) win over these, and a source missing here falls back to a per-kind built-in. Unknown keys are ignored.
_composio: A source spelled composio/<slug> — one of the services Composio brokers — falls back to this table's mcp/<slug> row when it has no composio/<slug> row of its own. The row answers a question about the SERVICE (how often does your GitHub change), not about the transport, and two copies of 77 rows would drift. learn/source_profile.py's table_entry is where that is done and why. Add a composio/<slug> key only when a brokered service genuinely differs from a dedicated server for it.
_mcp: Every mcp/* row ships with sync=false: a gather is the connection read through a fresh Hermes process on its own copy of the OAuth token, which is what cost this Mac its Cloudflare sign-in twice in a day, so nothing is polled until the person switches it on — and even then sync.sh gathers hourly at most, never every tick. dated=false because an auto-resolved read-set has no window in it; a hand recipe at ~/.moe/gather/<name>.json that puts {since_days} or {since_date} in an arg IS dated, and lib/mcp_autoread substitutes the window there.
_speak: Whether Moe may speak up about a source on its own: the proactive pass (hermes-jobs/moe-brief-monitor.sh drops the brief sections of a source whose speak is false) and a watch job. It follows the rest of the row rather than being an answer of its own — a source Moe keeps up with (sync), reads back (seed) or may watch is one it may mention; a reference service it never reads cannot surprise anyone, so it is false there. A person's own answer (consent.sh mode <source> speak no) wins over this, as over every other field.
